newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up after two-way trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up after two-way trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's gold market traded in tight ranges in two-way business on Wednesday before ending higher than New York's previous close, bullion dealers said.
"Trade in the morning and afternoon was constricted within a tight range, with Australian bids and Japanese selling interest," said one dealer.
Australian dealers were bidding at US$382.40/70 per ounce, probably on behalf of producers who were hedging, the dealer said.
Japanese traders on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange sold some gold on dollar/yen swings, another trader said.
Some speculators took profits when gold hit $383 per ounce, contributing to the tight range, traders said.
"People are trying to set the limit at this level," said one bullion dealer, noting that if gold broke through $383 per ounce, it would edge up to $385.
Dealers said some London firms were selling gold in afternoon trade to establish fresh short positions in case they saw a chance to buy in later shortcovering.
But Swiss players saw the market as technically bullish and bought healthy amounts, again restricting gold to a narrow range with lows at $382.25/55 and highs at $382.75/383.05, dealers said.
Physical gold demand had drooped once again on stronger prices, they said.
Bullion ended at $382.60/383.10 an ounce Wednesday against New York's $382.20/70 close on Tuesday.
Local gold ended HK$10 higher at HK$3,524 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -6.00 from its previous fix at -8.00
